messages:
matt: FYI - watchdog auto-cordoned 8 nodes in us-west-2 ~18:12 UTC after ECC/Xid spikes. Capacity drop ~20% for GPU pool. Filing here to decide suppression/heuristics.
infra-bot: [AUTODRAIN] job=watchdog-2026-05-02-18:12 triggered; nodes=[gpu-uw2-12,gpu-uw2-15,gpu-uw2-16,gpu-uw2-21,gpu-uw2-22,gpu-uw2-24,gpu-uw2-30,gpu-uw2-31]; reason="ecc_count>5 per 60s".
tara: ouch. were these errors concentrated to a single GPU slot per node or across all GPUs?
matt: nvml shows spikes mainly on slot 0/PCIe 0 on 6 of the nodes, the other slots report transient mem-corrected but low.
alex: rough idea: we currently treat any NVML ECC/Xid threshold hit as node-level fault and cordon+drain. that's aggressive for slot-local faults.
kevin: cost note: when we drain full nodes we trigger reserved-capacity shortfalls and scale up extra on Dedicated; that's a $$ hit. we need better discrimination.
sre-oncall: agree. suggestion: add slot-aware suppression window and a soft-cordon state so GPU-local fencing can happen before full node eviction.
tara: how would soft-cordon work? can we avoid eviction of critical pinned workloads? some customers pin latency models to those nodes.
alex: proposal (quick):
```
watchdog:
  failure_window: 60s          # sliding window for counts
  slot_threshold: 4          # errors on same GPU -> fence that device
  node_threshold: 8          # errors across devices -> node cordon
  suppression_window: 300s   # after a soft action, suppress further drains
  slo_exempt_label: "critical=true"  # don't evict pods with this label in slo_mode
  slo_mode: true             # opt-in SLO-aware behavior
```
kevin: suppression_window looks fine, but what about noisy bursts from firmware? we need backoff + exponential escalate if it repeats.
matt: exact logs pasted: "[nvml] GPU0 Xid 31, count=7 in 45s
[nvml] GPU1 corrected ECC 2 in 50s
[nvml] GPU2 ok" — I can share full dump to pastebin.
sre-oncall: short-term action: push patch to watchdog to treat slot_threshold first and do soft-cordon with a per-gpu fence command: `nvidia-smi --gpu=0 -r` (where supported) and only cordon node if either node_threshold met OR 2+ GPUs fenced within 5m.
tara: we also need a safe-ttl for suppression so repeated false positives don't keep nodes out long. maybe suppression_window + max_total_suppression=1h.
alex: agree. also add an integration test: simulate single-slot Xid bursts and ensure autoscaler continues scheduling non-latency batch jobs that are label=evictable.
kevin: log/telemetry ask: add a metric "watchdog.action_type" with tags {node, slot, reason} so billing/ops can track cost impact per action.
sre-oncall: I'll open an RFC PR with exact config changes and runbook edits. urgent patch (hotfix) to land today: change default to slot-aware soft-cordon.
matt: thanks. I'll collect the NVML dumps and annotate which pods were evicted on each node and attach. link: https://paste.redwood.internal/abc123 (private). :eyes:
infra-bot: [DEPLOY] patch/watchdog/slot-aware soft-cordon preflight passed in staging (smoke tests: gpu-fence, node-cordon logic).
tara: +1 for staging results. after hotfix we should run a controlled fault-injection across 3 nodes to validate no mass-drain.
kevin: please add cost dashboard alarm if drain rate > 5 nodes/hr in a region.
sre-oncall: will do. action items: 1) matt: upload logs + evicted-pod list 2) alex: RFC + e2e test 3) tara: plan fault-injection 4) kevin: cost alarm 5) infra-bot: enable metric tagging.
matt: on it. :wave:
